subject: Rollout safeguards, rollback hatch and migration playbook — check-in
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: ACME – proposed model swap (v2) next week — risks and exception asks

Hi team,

Quick summary: Acme (DEAL-4521) is planning to switch their production route from model-internal v1 to v2 on 2028-03-21 as part of our hosted API rollout. They asked for a two-week overlap where we serve both variants from the same route and guarantee no automatic fallback to smaller quantized variants.

Acme cites quality delta on a small set of prompts and wants us to avoid an automatic model downgrade during their initial cutover window. They’re also asking for retention of v1 KV caches for 14 days post-cutover.

As discussion points for this thread:
- Do we allow a customer-specific exception to the automatic fallback policy?
- Operational burden: what does supporting parallel model families on the same route cost (batching, GPU allocation, monitoring)?
- Comms cadence and runbook edits (canary, rollback steps).

I attached a draft migration_checklist.xlsx with fields I filled from the customer call. Can everyone flag the top three technical blockers by EOD?

Thanks —
Monica
Monica Patel
Senior AM, Mid Market
Redwood Inference
  
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-14T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ACME – proposed model swap (v2) next week — risks and exception asks

Monica — thanks for the write-up and checklist. High-level position: we can support a temporary overlap but it requires explicit operational controls and a documented rollback hatch — we should not change the global fallback policy. Notes below: 

Operational impact (quick):
- Serving: parallel model families on a single route will double KV-cache footprint and increase scheduling complexity; estimate +15–25% GPU utilization on affected nodes.
- Batching: mixing fwd pass shapes may reduce batching efficiency; expect ~8–12% latency regression at 95th perc during peak.
- Observability: we must create a per-model cost/latency dashboard and an error-regression alert tied to the canary. Hannah, can you scope the dashboard and alert SLA?

Proposed controls for a customer exception:
1) Explicit allowlist on routing policy for Acme only (timeboxed).
2) Canary: 5% of traffic to v2 for 24 hours, monitor objective function (latency + quality) then ramp.
3) Rollback hatch: automated immediate rollback to v1 if token loss > 1.5% or latency delta > 40% sustained 10m.
4) No change to global auto-fallback; exceptions logged and require a CS+ProdOps sign-off.

Attachments: I reviewed migration_checklist.xlsx and added an ops checklist tab. I also sketched a canary_runbook.md — attaching.

Action items:
- Hannah: dashboard & alert scope — EOD today.
- Aditya: feasibility on preserving KV cache snapshots and restoring them for the customer after cutover — estimate cost and storage.
- Ben: legal/commercial ask — confirm whether we can sign a short-term SLA addendum for overlap (customer expects written confirmation).

I’ll draft a one-page rollback + communications blurb for Acme once we have the technical OK.

—Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Product Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-14T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ACME – proposed model swap (v2) next week — risks and exception asks

On Wed, Mar 14, 2028 at 10:05 AM Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com> wrote:
> I’ll draft a one-page rollback + communications blurb for Acme once we have the technical OK.

Quick scope from Observability side:
- Deliverables: per-model latency/cost dashboard (route-level), quality-regression alerting (compare generation rates on the eval prompt set), and a KV cache size gauge across nodes.
- ETA: lightweight dashboards and a PagerDuty alert rule within 24 hours (by tomorrow 11:30 PDT) if we have the canary metrics instrumented.
- Requirements from Prod: a consistent canary tag on requests (add header X-Canary: acme-v2) and a short list of ~25 representative prompts from the customer for quality gating. Monica — can you get that?

Notes: I’ll add SUP-1234 on the canary incident runbook and link it to the alert. I estimate ~4 engineer-hours total for initial setup and another 2–3 for fine tuning during the ramp.

Cheers,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
SRE, Observability
From: Kevin Liu <kevin.liu@acme-data.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-14T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ACME – proposed model swap (v2) next week — risks and exception asks

Thanks Monica and team — appreciated. A few clarifications from our side: 
- The reason we asked for no automatic fallback is that v1 contains several task-specific prompt adaptations that v2 doesn’t mirror; a fallback creates noise in our quality metrics and breaks downstream scoring.
- We’re willing to sign a short amendment that covers the overlap and liability for that window. Can you confirm the rollback triggers and whether we can request cache preservation for 14 days?

We’re aiming for the cutover on 2028-03-21 14:00 UTC. If we can get the canary and rollback agreement documented by Friday 2028-03-16 we’ll proceed.

Kevin Liu
Director of ML Platforms 
Acme Data
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Kevin Liu <kevin.liu@acme-data.com>, Sonia Patel <sonia@bigretail.com>
Date: 2028-03-14T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ACME – proposed model swap (v2) next week — risks and exception asks

Summary and decisions (finalized):
1) Exception approved (timeboxed): allow temporary overlap for Acme from 2028-03-21T14:00 UTC to 2028-04-04T14:00 UTC. This is a customer-specific routing allowlist; global fallback policy remains unchanged.
2) Canary plan: 5% traffic to v2 for first 24h with header X-Canary: acme-v2; ramp to 25% over 48h pending no regressions. Hannah to create dashboards and SUP-1234 is the incident ticket.
3) Rollback hatch: automated rollback to v1 if any of the following are met for a sustained 10m window — token loss > 1.5%, latency P95 delta > 40%, or generation failure rate > 0.8%.
4) KV cache retention: Aditya to confirm feasibility; target: snapshot exports and preserve for 14 days. If full snapshots are cost-prohibitive, we’ll offer a staged restore plan (customer-funded).
5) Commercial: Ben — please prepare a short-term amendment (DocuSign) that covers overlap and operational responsibilities; aim to send signature request by 2028-03-15 EOD. Customer expects written confirmation.

Next steps & owners:
- Hannah: dashboards + alerting (ETA 2028-03-15 11:30 PDT) — link to SUP-1234.
- Aditya: KV snapshot feasibility + cost estimate (ETA 2028-03-15 EOD).
- Ben: amendment + DocuSign flow (ETA 2028-03-15 EOD).
- Monica: collect 25 representative prompts and confirm cutover timestamp with Acme.

I attached the final canary_runbook.md and the migration_checklist.xlsx (updated) and have a customer-facing one-pager draft in the body below to send once Ben confirms the amendment is en route.

--- customer-facing blurb (draft) ---
Redwood will perform a timeboxed dual-model deployment for Acme (v1 and v2) starting 2028-03-21 14:00 UTC. Initial canary: 5% traffic routed to v2. We will monitor quality and latency and will automatically rollback to v1 if defined thresholds are exceeded. A short-term amendment covering the overlap and operational responsibilities will be sent for signature.
--- end blurb ---

If there are no blockers, I will send the blurb to Kevin and attach the amendment link once Ben confirms.

—Markus
Head of Product Ops, Redwood Inference

Attachments: migration_checklist.xlsx; canary_runbook.md; customer_overlap_agreement.pdf
